method: Only question columns were read before answers. Answers use current canonical I/D/Q rules and their named child links; no original scores/reasons used. Model-layer questions deliberately require actual model evidence rather than inferring proof from ontology.

answers.question: Can we distinguish the child’s own success, its data and its missing audit row?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: The intended child record survives, keeps child Success provisionally and reads uncommitted when parent undoes it. Missing native audit row is not stated beside these rules; one needs metadata to know the as-built defect.

answers.question: Is loss on caller rollback a product fact or an approved policy?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: Caller rollback policy is explicitly provisional with alternatives; it is not owner-approved policy. The as-built lost-row observation is not stated in the Q itself.

answers.question: Can the model distinguish two child modes under the same parent?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: Ontology distinguishes child flags and normal parent behavior but cannot establish a Verus model input or theorem domain.

answers.question: Does the surviving write set follow the position of a process cut?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: Rule distinguishes mode and developer commit stage, but exact process cut write prefix and journal mode sequence require an actual model symbol.

answers.question: Is the late failure visible beside the normal rollback rule?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: Owning late-status rule says postcommit cleanup/message/history failure may report error while load is kept, but normal rollback table does not link the exception beside its row.

answers.question: Is the error outcome reachable after a successful final commit?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: Owning rule describes late failure but does not establish reachability in formal state machine.

answers.question: Does a whole-instance restart get its own persistence semantics?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: IRISTEMP and end copy stated; whole-instance restart semantics are not expressed by a dedicated owning case. Model evidence required.

answers.question: Would a plausible, wrong history-filter parser pass the same tests?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: Required filters and unknown-column uncertainty are stated. A parser mutant outcome cannot be established from ontology prose.

answers.question: Does a permitted delete always win against an in-progress writer?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: No: Q explicitly allows deletion and normal completion whether or not record returns. It leaves final-writer/delete outcome unresolved.

answers.question: What does the history bit promise about files?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: Open policy with working assumption DB-only; filesystem effects can survive independently. It does not promise all files restored or Committed bit accounts for them.

answers.question: Does rejecting a graph prove there is no legal version assignment?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: Intended conflict means no common satisfying version, but ordering defect is explicit in version.range.combine. This does not establish completeness of formal graph rejection.

answers.question: Can one namespace verify isolation between two namespaces?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: IDs scoped per namespace and separate logs are stated; one namespace model cannot establish a two-namespace comparison.

answers.question: Can the retry obligation be applied after an exact-byte revert?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: Rule says failed sync is retried but omits the exact-byte-revert exception/observed defect. A reader cannot predict this case from rule alone.

answers.question: Does the first developer commit change the outcome of a later failure?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: Rules distinguish before versus after first developer commit; proof of actual represented transition needs formal model.

answers.question: Do we distinguish the caller’s later rollback from the action’s own successful return?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: Caller later rollback explicitly differs from command return; formal caller state and outcome proof not established by prose.

answers.question: Does a claim about prior versions and dependency count match its quantified domain?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: No bound on dependency count or prior namespaces appears in operator rule; actual model theorem quantified domain must be read.

answers.question: Is the difference between an ordinary load and the Test phase explicit?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: Test-scoped resources/dependencies run only in Test, distinct from ordinary load phases.

answers.question: Does “normal load rolls back its dependencies” distinguish child defaults from parent flags?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: Yes: load.outcome links both child-default questions. Child NoJournal escapes parent journal rollback as working assumption; NoTransaction suppression is separate policy uncertainty.

answers.question: Will a reader know that the order of filter keys can change which records are deleted?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: No rule states lexicographic traversal stops at first invalid key, so valid keys before/after it have different effects. User cannot infer filter order deletion from owning statement.

answers.question: Are the global CLI view and programmatic query identified separately?
answers.answer_from_canonical_rules: CLI globally and programmatic GlobalRecords are named separately, but differing namespace selection/limits/row shape semantics are not stated in owning rules.
